Hi,
Not sure I see the benefit of this change at all. But why the name change to scopes? I feel that
does not reflect the purpose of beeing a memeory handler? To me wmem seems more fitting.

The motivation for the change is to use wmem outside of epan, in particular with wsutil, and avoid code duplication. `format_size()` is an example of that.

Scopes requires a bit of explanation. Scope management for epan used to be part of wmem. With the removal of wmem from epan the scope management (for epan) stayed in epan. That needs a name, can be any but best practice says it should not be "wmem" because that namespace belongs to wmem.

Same idea applies to the scope names: wmem_packet_scope(), etc. Formally it should have a different name that doesn't impinge on the wmem namespace.

Edit: `format_size()` was copied from wsutil to epan, but moving the other way is also possible, there are utility functions in epan that would be useful in wsutil, for byte formatting, etc, but they can't be moved currently because they use wmem.

Hi
Mem_scope? To make it clearer what type of scope it is?


skrev:

We can keep the existing names if it will make this more acceptable, there is some history there after all.

If I remove commit 7ef483a23a nothing much changes in the epan API and I can still achieve my goals.

At a high level this makes a lot of sense to me, thanks for doing it! At one point I'd actually wondered about extracting wmem to an entirely stand-alone library project so I could use it in something non-wireshark-related, but it never ended up being relevant.

I agree with Anders that "scopes" is not a clear name, I second "mem_scopes" as clearer.

Another thing that I thought about while skimming the diff was whether `in_scope` even really belongs inside the `wmem` library anymore? It's arguably not that relevant to wmem as a memory manager, and is more relevant to epan's use of it for scope management? But I'm not sure where else we'd put it, and the fact you moved the `wmem_free_all`s into `wmem_leave_scope` makes me feel a bit better about its integration.

In a similar vein, it feels really weird to be entering/leaving file scope in `packet.c` and entering/leaving packet scope in `epan.c`, that feels backwards to me. But the calls were already there, it just stands out now that we've put the methods there too.

The natural home for that assertion could be the acessor functions for scope allocators.
That makes sense, if it works. I have a vague feeling there are places calling the accessor methods outside of the scope, for use later when it's in scope, but I can't actually think of an example.
There are indeed. OK I will add the assertions back as they were before.

commits_data.title: Remove duplicate format_size() function
commits_data.message:
Remove duplicate format_size() function

We have two format_size()s, with and without wmem scoped memory.
Move the wmem version to wsutil and add a convenience macro to
use g_malloc()ed memory.

commits_data.title: Move epan/wmem/wmem_scopes.h to epan/
commits_data.message:
Move epan/wmem/wmem_scopes.h to epan/

This header was installed incorrectly to epan/wmem_scopes.h.

Instead of creating additional installation rules for a single
header in a subfolder (kept for backward compatibility) just
rename the standard "epan/wmem/wmem.h" include to
"epan/wmem_scopes.h" and fix the documentation.

Now the header is installed *correctly* to epan/wmem_scopes.h.

commits_data.title: Move wmem to wsutil
commits_data.message:
Move wmem to wsutil

This allows wmem to be used from other libraries, namely wsutil.
It is often the case that a funtion exists in wsutil and cannot
be used with a wmem scope, requiring some code duplication or
extra memory allocations, or vice-versa, code in epan cannot be
moved to wsutil because it has a wmem dependency.

To this end wmem is moved to wsutil. Scope management remains part
of epan because those scope semantics are specific to dissection.
